A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the economics of professional football is a complex and multi-faceted subject that requires an interdisciplinary approach.
economic analysis is not a substitute for, but a useful complement to, the broader social science perspective.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the economic analysis of sport and the wider leisure industry is not the sole means of addressing the problems that face it, and that a broader perspective is required.
economic analysis of professional sport should not be conducted in isolation, but rather should be part of a broader analysis that incorporates the cultural and political aspects of the sport.
the economic approach is not the only one available to the study of football, nor should it be the dominant one.
